ai.description: This 3–4 cm frog has a stout, globular body with a mottled brown or grey dorsum. It features a shovel-shaped metatarsal tubercle for burrowing and a distinct, rounded snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: Distinguish *Sphaerotheca pluvialis* by the presence of a distinct, shovel-shaped, black-tipped inner metatarsal tubercle on each hind foot, used for efficient burrowing.
ai.habitat: Jerdon's burrowing frog inhabits deciduous forests and scrublands across the Indian subcontinent, typically found in moist soil at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: Jerdon’s burrowing frogs remain dormant underground for most of the year, emerging only during monsoon rains to breed and forage in temporary pools.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Sphaerotheca pluvialis* breeds during the monsoon, laying hundreds of eggs in small, temporary rain pools. Females deposit clutches in gelatinous masses in the water.
ai.distributionRemarks: Jerdon's burrowing frog is found across peninsular India, primarily in the Western Ghats and Deccan Plateau, ranging from sea level up to 1,000 meters in elevation.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Sphaerotheca pluvialis* is a series of low-pitched, metallic "tuk-tuk" notes heard from shallow, rain-filled pools during the monsoon season.
